newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog closes down Manchester stockbrokers.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog closes down Manchester stockbrokers.

text.p: British financial watchdog the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) on Friday ordered Manchester-based stockbrokers John Siddall and Son Ltd to cease trading for failing to maintain adequate financial resources.

The firm was reprimanded in June and two of its directors, Stephen Alexander and Gregory Banks were expelled for deceiving it over matters concerning dealings for a client in Anglia Television Group shares in 1994.

The SFA said in a statement it had been necessary for it to issue the order for the firm to cease trading immediately and to arrange for clients and the management of their accounts to be transferred to another firm.
It said Siddall and Son had failed to ensure it maintained externally generated group financial resources in excess of its group financial resources requirement.
The firm had also failed to comply with and SFA direction in December 1996 and to maintain financial resources in excess of its financial resources requirements, the SFA added.

And while the firm had informed the SFA it would rectify the problems, on July 22 the SFA discovered funds which Siddall had said were available to use as regulatory capital had in fact been transferred to a client account.
